object_description: compact two-storey facility integrating three uses under one roof
design_condition: The compact facility is positioned as an island at the edge of the landscape chamber, preserving views toward the historic ensemble while defining the southern end of the slope and connecting to the wider path network.

positive.statement: The site-specific positioning preserves views into the landscape and convincingly clarifies the landscape situation.

position.rationale: The compact building occupies the southern edge, leaving the landscape-facing side open.

positive.statement: Integrating the three uses under one roof creates a compact, self-evident overall unit.

position.rationale: The continuous sampled envelope clearly reads as one compact large-form building.

positive.statement: The new promenade integrates the complex into the wider path network.

position.rationale: The promenade is not distinct in the cloud and is estimated along the southern approach.

positive.statement: The landscaping provides spacious, freely configurable recreational and play areas.

position.rationale: Open recreation space is estimated beyond the building's northern landscape-facing edge.

positive.statement: The terraced classroom structure gives the classes a recognizable identity.

position.rationale: Repeated stepped traces along the eastern portion suggest the classroom structure.

positive.statement: The sequence from entrance through group rooms, classroom, and garden reflects this individual identity.

position.target: sequence from entrance through rooms, classroom, and garden
position.rationale: The internal sequence is approximated along the building's longitudinal depth toward the landscape edge.

positive.statement: The architectural expression adequately structures the volume and corresponds to the scale of the overall composition.

position.rationale: The stepped roofline and unified envelope visibly structure the overall volume.

positive.statement: The structural design is careful, clear, and easy to implement.

position.rationale: Structure is not separately visible, so it is anchored within the eastern building mass.

positive.statement: The project establishes an appropriate dialogue with the historic complex without competing with it.

position.rationale: The southern face is the likely interface toward the historic ensemble and wider landscape.

positive.statement: The approach to the landscape and children's needs is sensitive across the entire perimeter.

position.target: approach to landscape and children's needs
position.rationale: Perimeter landscape is estimated around the building's northern and eastern edges.

positive.statement: The chosen construction achieves the grey-energy target and required daylight quotient.

position.rationale: Sustainability and daylight performance are whole-building judgments without a specific location.

negative.statement: The shared entrance is problematic because the primary school lacks an identifiable communal entrance space.

position.rationale: The shared entrance is approximated at the southern central edge of the unified building.

negative.statement: The northern corridor cannot sufficiently support cross-cutting activities.

position.rationale: The corridor is estimated along the building's northern interior edge.

negative.statement: The intervention in the slope with high retaining walls is not mature enough.

position.rationale: Retaining walls are estimated at the southern slope intervention beneath the building.

negative.statement: The parking arrangement is unsatisfactory for creating an address.

position.rationale: Parking is absent from the cloud and estimated near the southern approach.

negative.statement: The compact classroom structure lacks flexibility and independence between individual rooms.

position.rationale: Classroom organization is approximated in the stepped eastern portion of the building.

negative.statement: The interior group rooms cannot be used independently and lack an appropriate connection to the outside.

position.rationale: Group rooms are not distinguishable and are estimated near the northern landscape-facing side.

negative.statement: A view from the hall level into the landscape would have been desirable.

position.rationale: The hall is approximated on the southern side facing the landscape.

negative.statement: The castle-garden design remains questionable in terms of its fit with the garden's significance.

position.rationale: The significant garden is not represented distinctly and is estimated beyond the northern building edge.

negative.statement: The all-weather square requires an unsightly cut into the topography.

position.rationale: The square is absent from the sample and estimated within the southern topographic approach.

negative.statement: The bulkhead structure of the basic level restricts flexibility of use.

position.target: bulkhead structure of the basic level
position.rationale: The basic level is approximated in the lower southern portion of the compact mass.

negative.statement: The moderate window proportion and orientation limit solar gains.

position.rationale: Window rhythm is visible along the southern and eastern elevations.

negative.statement: The untreated timber façade is only partially protected from weathering.

position.rationale: The southern facade is directly represented across the long elevation.

negative.statement: The relatively large floor area results in only average cost-effectiveness.

position.rationale: Cost-effectiveness is a whole-building performance judgment without a spatial referent.

negative.statement: The internal organization of the basic level has conceptual shortcomings that preclude the desired spatial and usage flexibility.

position.target: internal organization of the basic level
position.rationale: The basic-level organization is estimated within the lower central building zone.
